detail.longDescription: I am using WSL2 to connect to a remote machine via SSH. I am running a Docker container on that remote machine with bind mounts that I want to hot-reload from host to container or vice versa, but neither is working. The file changes are not received in either direction. Topology : Window's Terminal running WSL2, connecting via SSH to a remote machine running Ubuntu. Let's refer to this remote machine as the Client . NOTE: VS Code is not involved whatsoever, nor do I want to use VS Code. I do know, however, that if I connect to the Client using VS Code's Remote SSH extension, the problem I am having does not occur. In fact, within that topology, all my Docker bind mounts are hot-reloadable without the need for any special watchers; it just works. If possible, I would like to replicate that behavior within my current topology (see Topology above). Aim : Run a Docker container on the Client whose bind mounts are all hot-reloadable. That is, whose edits on the Client are reflected in the running image or, conversely, whose edits within the container are reflected on the Cilent . Minimal reproducible example : Let's assume we are on the Client as defined in Topology . Then, run any Docker image compatible with the following invocation: docker run -it --entrypoint /bin/bash -v /home/user/<some_file>:/workspace/<some_file> where <some_file> can be any editable file. With the container running, edit <some_file> on the Client or within the container. Save the edit and observe that the other side's version of the file does not receive the update.
